mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate above 4.2% triggers a loss of investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite UNRATE crossing the threshold, or the effect persists beyond 20 days without reversal.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and growth in GDP (GDPC1) signals a dual easing of monetary policy and robust demand, amplifying equity valuation appreciation and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing combined with strong demand
failure_condition: The two proxies move in opposite directions or the 20-day returns are not significantly positive relative to a baseline of similar dual movements.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly increase in GDP growth (GDPC1) over three months indicates expanding economic activity, boosting corporate earnings expectations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns fail to outperform a 95% confidence interval around baseline returns during periods of similar GDP growth trends.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion phase characterized by sustained GDP growth (GDPC1 > 23536), the S&P 500 experiences positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days as market anticipates peak growth.
failure_condition: The 60-day returns fail to be significantly positive during periods when GDPC1 exceeds 23536, or the effect diminishes in subsequent quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment (UNRATE) and labor demand (HOUST) signals labor market tightness and potential wage inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.1pp and HOUST rises > 1000 in the same month
failure_condition: The 5-day returns do not turn negative when both UNRATE and HOUST meet the trigger conditions, or the effect reverses quickly.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105 indicates overcapacity and potential economic slowdown, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day returns remain non-negative despite INDPRO crossing the 105 threshold, or the effect persists beyond 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of ultra-low unemployment (UNRATE < 3.5%) and accommodative monetary policy (FEDFUNDS < 4%), the S&P 500 experiences positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days as market confidence surges.
regime_hint: ultra-low unemployment and loose monetary policy
failure_condition: The 60-day returns fail to be significantly positive when both UNRATE and FEDFUNDS meet the trigger conditions, or the effect reverses in subsequent periods.
